summary: Dennis Hirota specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a B.A. and M.A. from UC Berkeley and a Ph.D. from Nagoya University. He served at the Hongwanji International Center around 1977 and became a professor at Ryukoku University around 1996.

Derek F. Maher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, completing his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins. He lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, and co-directed the Religious Studies Program at East Carolina University.

Dermot Killingley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford and SOAS University of London. He held a post at the University of Malaya (1967-1970) before serving as Senior Lecturer and Reader at Newcastle University (circa 1970-2000).

Dermott Joseph Walsh specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his BA at Trinity College Dublin in 2003, an MA at Leiden University in 2009, and a PhD in 2018 from UCLA under doctoral supervisor William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramkrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911-1917) and Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen and committee member Leo K. Shin.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Gatön Ngawang Lekpa, Ngawang Nyima, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington from 1960 to 1972.
Dhammanandā is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the doctoral supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe.
Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Hong Kong under K. L. Dhammajoti. He later served as a guest assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Dhirendra Mohan Datta was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta from circa 1917 to 1923. He held posts at Patna College in 1928 and the University of Minnesota from 1951 to 1952.
Dhirendra Sharma was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He served as an associate lecturer at the Open University and held a post at the University of Chester in 2019.

Di Luo specializes in Sinology, archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Southern California under doctoral supervisors Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge.
Diana L. Eck is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard University. She became a professor at Harvard University circa 1976.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She has served as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford, and later held posts at Pepperdine University, Kenyon College, and Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who was a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen.
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at the École Polytechnique under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.
Diego Loukota works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA at Peking University and a PhD in 2019 at the University of California, Los Angeles.
